recommendation: Keep this no-change audit. If a future core build surface shows the old unconfirmed definition, fix the THO dependency/build input or generated publication process rather than reintroducing a core CodeSystem source file.
issue_request: FHIR-32479 was an Applied/Persuasive with Modification Patient Care change request for the Condition verification status unconfirmed code. It requested replacing the tautological definition with "There is not sufficient evidence to assert the presence of the subject's condition."
initial_application: No Jira-tagged core source commit for FHIR-32479 was found. The core-owned condition-ver-status CodeSystem duplicate had already been removed by the December 2022 THO-duplicate cleanup before the Jira resolution was applied, and the implementation path was the UTG/THO proposal UP-387.
additional_context: UP-387 is Proposal Implemented and records the Patient Care-approved definitions for both unconfirmed and confirmed. FHIR-32480 is the companion confirmed-code issue and is already represented on the combined branch. Current core source keeps the active Condition binding and ValueSet include, while the CodeSystem OID is commented in source/oids.ini, confirming the code definitions are not active core source.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. A core source edit would recreate or modify terminology that now belongs to THO; the current authoritative THO CodeSystem already contains the requested unconfirmed definition.

related_jiras.note: Companion Applied issue for the confirmed code, implemented through the same UP-387 terminology proposal and already audited on the combined branch.
